intent: Baseline geometry: five 12 mm sensors at 10 mm pitch, centred and 5 cm ahead of the axle, on a 12 cm track with 3 cm wheels and 0.8 kg mass. I kept it mid-range everywhere so the Integrator has a balanced platform. I am considering, but not yet committing to, a shorter sensor lead (about 6 to 7 cm) if the Integrator reports oscillation at speed, and a wider sensor spread (about 3 cm either side) if the robot loses the line in tight bends. The expected result is a completed run at moderate speed with small rms_error. This is not yet verified.
learning: Baseline only. Next iteration, use the race telemetry (rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation) and the Integrator's notes on sensor saturation or line loss to decide whether to widen the sensor spread, move the sensors forward or back, or change the track and mass.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no Integration Feedback and no Geometry Race Data, so there is no evidence yet to favour one geometry over another. I am proposing a conservative baseline. Five sensors across the front, spaced 10 mm apart and centred on the robot, cover the 25 mm tape with some overlap. That gives a smooth, roughly linear signal near the line centre and keeps at least two sensors on the tape through moderate bends. The 12 mm footprint gives a good trade-off between signal smoothness and sensitivity to the line edge. Sensors sit 5 cm ahead of the axle so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it, which helps at speed. The 12 cm wheel track and 3 cm wheel radius are mid-range values that give stable yaw response without sluggish turning. Mass is 0.8 kg, and the 12 cm body width keeps the off-track limit at 6 cm, which is the floor and so a generous margin. I expect a completion with a modest line error, to be confirmed or revised once the race returns data.
